kinds.name: channel_echo
kinds.doc: Starts a channel that sends back every message it is given.

slots.name: start
slots.doc:
A channel whose every message comes back through `sink`, in order,
from a thread of the provider's own where it has one.

`config` may say `close_after` (a count: after echoing that many
messages the provider closes the stream itself) and `close_status`
(the status it closes with then; `0` when left out) and
`close_reason` (the text it closes with then; empty when left out).
When the host closes, the echo passes the host's status and reason
on to the sink.

kinds.name: channel
kinds.doc:
What the host writes on, handed back by the provider that started it.

The provider implements it and the host holds the channel object,
which may be shared between threads: `send` may be called from several
at once, each thread's messages kept in its own order. Dropping the
channel is `close(GUATIAO_OK, "")`.

slots.name: send
slots.doc:
One message to the provider, lent for the call. Returns once the
provider has taken it, which may wait on the provider; answers
`GUATIAO_ERR_GONE` once either side has closed, and a `send` that
was waiting when the host closed answers it too.

slots.name: close
slots.doc:
Ends the stream from the host's side, with a `guatiao_status` the
provider hands to the sink's `closed`: `GUATIAO_OK` (0) for a plain
end, an error status otherwise. `reason` is UTF-8 text for people,
lent for the call and empty when there is none: why the host gives
up. Called once, and returns without waiting for a `receive` still
running; `send` answers `GUATIAO_ERR_GONE` after it. Cannot fail,
bar a `reason` that is not UTF-8, which is refused with
`GUATIAO_ERR_BAD_VALUE` before this runs and leaves the stream as
it was.

kinds.name: channel_sink
kinds.doc:
What the provider writes back on, handed in by the host.

The host implements it and hands it over with the call that starts
the channel; the provider owns it from then on, makes every call on it
from one thread at a time, and destroys it when done.

slots.name: receive
slots.doc:
One message to the host, lent for the call. Returns once the host
has taken it, and a host never waits in it for its own `send`.
`GUATIAO_ERR_GONE` says the host takes nothing more; any error
ends the stream, and the provider then calls `closed` with that
status and delivers nothing still queued.

slots.name: closed
slots.doc:
The stream has ended, from either side: with the host's status from
the channel's `close`, or the provider's own, a `guatiao_status`
(`GUATIAO_OK` is the normal end). `reason` is UTF-8 text for
people, lent for the call and empty when there is none: the
provider's failure, or the host's reason passed on. Called exactly
once, and nothing but `destroy` follows it. Cannot fail, bar a
`reason` that is not UTF-8, which is refused with
`GUATIAO_ERR_BAD_VALUE` before this runs and leaves the stream as
it was.
